title: Hamilton should have referenced Great Comet tbh #broadway #musicalthe...
transcript: Did you know that Natasha Pierre and the Great Comet of 1812 very briefly had a Hamilton reference? Great Comet does technically predate Hamilton by a couple of years. It had two very successful runs in New York in 2012 and 2013 before Hamilton premiered in 2015. But in between their off Broadway runs and their somewhat ill-fated Broadway run in 2017, they played a tryout production at A.R.T in Massachusetts. This was in December of 2015, at the peak of Hamilton mania. And so I guess they decided to include a little Easter egg. It happened in Act 1 during the number The Duel. Of course, fitting, because Hamilton famously also features a few duels. And at that moment in the Cambridge production, the synths in the underscoring played the duel motif from Hamilton. In the absence of a slime tutorial, if I may, it went a little something like: well,let's begin. This is child's play. At first I thought I might have imagined it, but I did confirm it from the man himself. At intermission, I was talking to Mr. Dave Malloy. Casual! I worked with him once. What? And I was like, hey, Dave, was that a… Was that a Hamilton reference in The Duel? And he was like, “yeah, it was a little Easter egg.” But for better or for worse, they did in fact take it out for the Broadway production. As much as it was fun to experience that, I am glad they took it out. In fairness, Great Comet does exist in a sort of heightened, self aware reality that can accommodate a sort of 4th-wall break like this. But during this time when everyone and their mother was referencing Hamilton left and right, it felt ever so slightly beneath them to jump on that bandwagon and invite those comparisons when Great Comet is a staggering work of genius in its own right and deserve to stand on its own feet. And those of us in favor of a Lin Manuel and Dave Malway crossover only had to wait.
